extracted.intended_audience: users and contributors to the AoPS Wiki (students and other site users learning to create/edit pages)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating, editing, and maintaining articles on the Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) Wiki, including syntax, linking, finding pages to work on, and community netiquette. Aimed at new and intermediate contributors learning the platform's conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing the AoPS Wiki (general encouragement and constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AoPS Wiki is meant to be edited by you, the users! We encourage you to modify and enhance the AoPS Wiki. To edit an article, however, you must first be familiar with the AoPS Wiki's operational procedures. Also, please do not randomly edit things for no reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contribute improvements, but learn the procedures before editing; avoid pointless or random edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning About AoPS Wiki (explore to understand structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: All users are encouraged to read up on what a wiki is and look around AoPS Wiki. Click the Random Page button ... to get a feel for the structure of content in the AoPS Wiki. Try clicking through a few of the colored links on some of the pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore Random Page and internal links to see how articles are organized; read 'what makes the AoPS Wiki different'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating an Article (when a topic is missing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you search a topic or click on a link to an article that was not yet written, you yourself can begin creating that article. It is preferred to make bold the name of the article when it first appears in the article, particularly for terms that are given definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating a new article, bold the article name at first occurrence; consult 'Tips for Article Creation' to understand AoPS Wiki philosophy; consider expanding stubs if you can't think of a topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing an Article (how to start editing existing or new pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Click on the (Edit) button above an article while you are logged into the AoPS Wiki. If the article is new, you can just start writing. If the article already exists, you will see the article text, MediaWiki syntax included. Write around or over the text to change the content of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Edit button while logged in; when unsure, experiment in the Sandbox to test syntax and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sandbox usage (experiment safely)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you would like to experiment with the Wiki format, please use the Sandbox to play around with new features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice syntax and formatting in your user page or the Sandbox rather than on live articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wiki syntax — bullets, indent, italic, bold
rubrics_metrics.description: Here are a few common ways to format content in your article: To create bullets ... use the asterisk (*) at the beginning of each line. Use the colon (:) to indent. To italicize text, place two apostrophes both before and after the ''text''. To bold text, place three apostrophes both before and after the '''text'''.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these simple MediaWiki syntaxes for common formatting instead of HTML when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal links (use [[...]] and piped links for display text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place two square brackets on each side of a word or phrase to link the text to the article of the same name. For example, to create the link mathematics, type [[mathematics]]. Use piped links like [[real number|reals]] to link to a differently-named article but show alternate text. To link to a specific section, use [[Article#Section|display text]].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer internal links for wiki navigation; use piped links to control displayed text; link to sections via # when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: External links (formatting and protocol shorthand)
rubrics_metrics.description: When linking to information outside of the AoPS Wiki, use external links. Begin with one open square bracket, type or paste the URL replacing http(s):// with //, add a space, then type the text that should appear naming the external link. For example: [//www.maa.org Mathematical Association of America]. Note that https://artofproblemsolving.com can be replaced with {{SERVER}}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single-bracket external-link format and protocol-less URLs (//); consult 'AoPS Wiki:Linking books' before adding external links to books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redirects (creating redirect pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an article has several less standard names or acronyms, you can create a page (or pages) to direct users who find each one to the article name you chose. Example: #REDIRECT[[American Regions Mathematics League]].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create redirect pages for common alternate names/acronyms; use redirects instead of duplicate content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Templates and Categories (use and consult guides)
rubrics_metrics.description: See the article templates and categories for a definitive guide on creating and using templates & categories, as well as a list of templates and categories currently in existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use existing templates and categories to maintain consistency; consult the respective help pages for how to create/use them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding Articles To Edit — Red Links
rubrics_metrics.description: If you notice a red internal link, that represents an article that has not yet been written. Click on the red link to start writing that article. Remember that the article on this subject may have already been written under a slightly different name, so it is always a good idea to make a little search first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for alternate names before creating a new article; create a redirect page if the relevant article exists under a different name; check red link text for spelling before creating the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding Articles To Edit — Recent Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recently changed articles are usually fairly new articles. You can find recently changed articles by clicking on the Recent Changes link ... Go methodically through the articles, either contributing or adding broken links. Also see the Community Portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Recent Changes to find new or unstable articles to improve; systematically work through changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding Articles To Edit — Wanted Pages
rubrics_metrics.description: The AoPS Wiki automatically creates a list of wanted pages. These are pages to which there exist several links, but no actual page exists. This is a good place to look for articles which would contribute the most to the AoPS Wiki's goodness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target wanted pages as high-impact contribution opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding Articles To Edit — Stubs
rubrics_metrics.description: Many short articles are deemed stubs and have text saying 'This article is a stub. Help us by expanding it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended that users expand stubs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice Good Netiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolutely no spam is permitted on the AoPS Wiki. Practice good netiquette. Be aware of what the AoPS Wiki is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid spam and inappropriate content; follow community norms and be mindful of the wiki's purpose and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to Ask Questions — AoPS Forums / Site Support
rubrics_metrics.description: The AoPS Forums are the appropriate place to ask questions about AoPS, mathematics, concepts, specific math problems, and problem solving. The Site Support forum is a place to ask questions about AoPS Wiki and its functionality when you cannot find the explanation in the AoPS Wiki itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read announcements and sticky threads in Site Support before posting; use forum search to find answers; use appropriate forum sections for topic type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article Discussion (use the Discussion tab)
rubrics_metrics.description: Click the Discussion tab at the top of an article to ask questions about the article or discuss its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the article's Discussion page to coordinate improvements or raise content questions specific to that article.
